name: Firefox
summary: A multi-process Gecko browser that separates browser, content, GPU, socket, and media roles, transforms web documents through DOM/style/layout and WebRender boundaries, and uses IPDL plus sandbox policies for controlled communication and failure handling.
scope: DOM, style, layout, and WebRender pipeline

features.name: Gecko process hierarchy and isolation
features.description: Firefox documents a parent process that creates content, GPU, socket, data-decoder, and other child process types. Content processes separate web HTML and JavaScript from browser authority, while process selection and sandboxing vary by role and platform.
benefits: Separates web content and unstable system components from browser control
Allows role-specific sandbox and resource policies
costs: More processes increase memory and launch coordination cost
Platform-specific process availability complicates lifecycle reasoning

features.name: Gecko DOM, style, layout, and WebRender pipeline
features.description: Gecko separates DOM and style data from layout evaluation and graphics composition. The layout and graphics documentation describes derived geometry and display structures that feed compositor and WebRender paths, rather than treating the DOM as final pixels.
benefits: Makes document structure, computed style, geometry, and display work separable
Allows graphics backends to consume derived display representations
costs: Invalidation across DOM, style, layout, and graphics stages is expensive to coordinate
Backend and platform differences remain visible at the rendering boundary

features.name: IPDL actor protocol boundary
features.description: Firefox uses IPDL to describe typed parent/child actors and asynchronous inter-thread or inter-process messages. Top-level actors establish process connections, while endpoints and actor lifetimes make communication ownership explicit.
benefits: Provides generated protocol structure for process and thread communication
Makes actor ownership, message direction, and shutdown behavior reviewable
costs: Protocol evolution and actor teardown add lifecycle complexity
Incorrect synchronous or re-entrant communication can threaten responsiveness or deadlock safety

features.name: Browser-owned network and storage service boundaries
features.description: Firefox gives networking and persistent web storage dedicated service and process boundaries. Socket-process communication, DOM storage/Quota ownership, and content-to-parent actors keep renderer-like content from directly owning all network or profile state.
benefits: Centralizes profile, quota, network, and policy decisions
Provides explicit boundaries for asynchronous I/O and durable web state
costs: Actors and service processes add latency and failure propagation paths
Storage partitioning, quota, and profile lifecycle require coordinated ownership

features.name: Sandboxed process shutdown and crash model
features.description: Firefox assigns sandbox policies to process roles and documents explicit process shutdown handling. Parent actors observe child exits and IPC failure, allowing browser state to distinguish normal teardown from crashed or disconnected content and service processes.
benefits: Reduces authority of content and specialized child processes
Makes crash, channel closure, and orderly shutdown part of process lifecycle handling
costs: Sandbox policy and brokered access are platform-specific maintenance surfaces
Recovering from child loss can discard in-flight work and require state reconstruction

mathematical_views.question: How do parent, content, GPU, socket, and media processes connect, and which roles may create or communicate with one another?
assumptions: Process roles are graph nodes and IPDL actors are labeled edges
Platform-specific process folding is represented as a graph variation rather than ignored

mathematical_views.question: Which transitions transform DOM and style changes into layout geometry, display structures, and compositor/WebRender work?
assumptions: DOM, style, layout, and display representations are distinct states
Invalidation and refresh scheduling are labeled transitions
The model abstracts GPU commands and pixel-level rendering behavior

mathematical_views.model: Actor protocol and failure transition system
mathematical_views.question: How do IPDL actor creation, message delivery, channel closure, child crash, and shutdown alter browser state?
assumptions: Actors and endpoints define communication state
Message delivery and actor destruction are observable transitions
The model abstracts OS-specific crash reporting and restart policy

costs: Process count and platform-specific lifecycle complexity
Actor lifetime and protocol evolution burden

benefits: Centralized profile and asynchronous I/O authority
Reduced child authority and explicit recovery states
